questions.question: Which of the following is a behavioural adaptation that helps an animal survive in its environment?
options: Having thick fur to trap heat
Being active only at night (nocturnal)
Having sharp claws to catch prey
Possessing large ears to lose heat

questions.question: Why is maintaining a high level of biodiversity crucial for ecosystems?
options: It ensures that only one dominant species survives.
It helps to maintain healthy, stable habitats.
It decreases the overall mass of living organisms.
It makes food chains much shorter and simpler.

questions.question: What is meant by the term "gene pool" in a species?
options: The total number of individuals living in a specific habitat.
The range of DNA and genetic information within a species.
The physical area where a species goes to find water.
The artificial storage of seeds in a seed bank.

questions.question: Which of the following is a method used to maintain and protect global biodiversity?
options: Encouraging deforestation for new farmland.
Introducing invasive species to new habitats.
Using gene banks to store genetic material.
Increasing the usage of chemical pesticides.

questions.question: Why do scientists use sampling to study populations in a large area rather than counting every individual?
options: Sampling takes more time but is always 100% accurate.
It would be practically impossible to count every single organism in an area.
Sampling guarantees that no organisms are harmed during the study.
It is only done when there are no living animals in the habitat.

questions.question: Which piece of equipment is a square frame used to sample plants or slow-moving animals?
options: A pitfall trap
A quadrat
A sweep net
A pooter

questions.question: Why is it important that quadrat sampling is usually done randomly?
options: To ensure that only the rarest plants are counted.
To avoid bias in the results.
To make the physical work easier for researchers.
To guarantee that every single quadrat contains organisms.

questions.question: What tool can be used by scientists and students to identify different, unfamiliar species in a habitat?
options: A classification key
A quadrat frame
A pyramid of biomass
A gene bank database

questions.question: An ecosystem is best described as which of the following?
options: Only the non-living parts of an environment like rocks and water.
A community of organisms interacting with each other and their non-living surroundings.
A collection of animals of the same species living together in a zoo.
The total number of plants growing in a specific region without any animals.

questions.question: What ecological role do the remains of dead organisms and waste products play in a habitat?
options: They have no purpose and must be removed to keep the habitat healthy.
They act as a direct barrier to prevent new plants from growing.
They provide a vital source of food for other organisms.
They are only used by carnivores to build shelters.

questions.question: Why do all living organisms depend on decomposers?
options: Decomposers produce oxygen through photosynthesis.
Decomposers are the primary source of prey for top predators.
Decomposers break down dead material and recycle useful substances for reuse.
Decomposers prevent herbivores from eating too many producers.

questions.question: What does the term "biodiversity" measure?
options: The total mass of a single species in an area.
The range of different living organisms in an area.
The speed at which energy moves through a food chain.
The physical size of the largest organism in a habitat.

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical adaptation of a plant designed to deter consumers?
options: Having wide, flat leaves to capture maximum sunlight.
Growing roots deep into the ground to find water.
The presence of sharp spines on the stems or leaves.
Releasing seeds that can float away in the wind.

questions.question: Which of these is a behavioural adaptation shown by plants?
options: Growing towards a light source.
Having thick bark to survive cold winters.
Growing long taproots to reach deep water.
Producing poisonous chemicals in their leaves.

questions.question: What is meant by the term "biomass"?
options: The total number of individual organisms in a habitat.
The mass of living material in one or more organisms.
The speed at which energy is transferred between trophic levels.
The volume of water contained within a single plant cell.

questions.question: What does a pyramid of biomass represent?
options: The number of individual organisms at each stage of a food chain.
The mass of living material at each stage of a food chain.
The height of different plants in a forest ecosystem.
The amount of non-living material in a habitat.

questions.question: In a pyramid of biomass, which organism is always represented by the bar at the very bottom?
options: The top predator
The secondary consumer
The primary consumer
The producer

questions.question: What is represented by a pyramid of number?
options: The estimated mass of all living things at each trophic level.
The physical size of each organism in a food chain.
The number of organisms at each trophic level in a food chain.
The number of different species in a whole country.
